accepted.question_text: When can a non-trivial virtual knot arise as the connected sum of two trivial virtual knots? Equivalently, for long virtual knots whose closure is the unknot, classify which non-isotopic long virtual knots can close to the same trivial compact knot and thereby explain when different connected-sum choices for closed virtual knots can produce a non-trivial result.

evidence.quote: Classify when a non-trivial virtual knot can be the connected sum of two trivial virtual knots.

With long virtual knots, the connected sum is ordered but well-defined, and the last question is closely related to the question of classifying the different long virtual knots whose closures are equivalent to the unknot.

accepted.question_text: Find new combinatorial invariants of flat virtual knots, and determine richer algebraic structures that can detect flat virtual-knot phenomena beyond mod 2 linking numbers despite the fact that the flat biquandle algebra is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra and has no non-trivial finite-dimensional representations.

evidence.quote: Flat virtual knots, also known as virtual strings [64, 214], are difficult to classify. Find new combinatorial invariants of flat virtual knots.
We would like to know more about the flat biquandle algebra. This algebra is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra [55] and has no (non-trivial) finite dimensional representations.

accepted.question_text: For the flat hierarchy in which flat crossings are labeled by elements of an ordinal alpha and a flat third Reidemeister move allows a strand with two labels a to slide across a crossing labeled b only when a is greater than b, classify the resulting diagrams and determine how this hierarchy generalizes ordinary flat virtual-knot theory.

evidence.quote: The flat hierarchy is constructed for any ordinal alpha.
In a flat third Reidemeister move, a line with two a labels can slide across a crossing labeled b only if a is greater than b.
Classify the diagrams in this hierarchy.

accepted.question_text: Clarify the relationship between flat virtual-knot theories and theories of doodles, including doodles with virtual crossings, and determine the resulting structures for cobordism, associated groups, and free-abelian cobordism classes of immersed surfaces without triple points.

evidence.quote: Virtuals and the Theory of Doodles: Compare flat theories of virtual knots with theories of doodles.
Cobordism of doodles is defined by an immersed surface without triple points. Cobordism classes represent elements of a free abelian group.
For example there is no reason not to have virtual crossings as well as flat crossings.

accepted.question_text: Do the two equivalence relations on ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed links - homeomorphism and virtual equivalence via generalized Kirby moves - actually coincide? More generally, give a geometric-topological interpretation of virtual 3-manifolds, and determine whether the alternative construction obtained by doing surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g x R up to stabilization yields the same theory.

evidence.quote: Do these equivalences coincide? That is, given two ordinary three manifolds, presented by surgery on framed links K and L, suppose that K and L are equivalent through the virtual Kirby calculus. Does this imply that they are equivalent through the classical Kirby calculus?
What is a virtual 3-manifold?: That is, give an interpretation of these equivalence classes in the domain of geometric topology.

Construct another theory of virtual 3-manifolds by performing surgery on links in thickened surfaces Sg x R considered up to stabilization. Will this theory coincide to that proposed by Kauffman and Dye [36]?

accepted.question_text: Develop effective invariants and, if possible, a classification theory for welded knots. In particular, determine whether Satoh's map from welded knots or links to ambient-isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space is faithful, and determine whether a welded knot with trivial fundamental group must itself be trivial as a welded knot.

evidence.quote: The question is to construct good invariants of welded knots and, if possible, to classify them.
Is this Satoh mapping faithful from equivalence classes of welded knots (links) to ambient isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space?
If a welded knot has trivial fundamental group, does this imply that the knot is trivial as a welded knot?

accepted.question_text: Strengthen the invariant theory for long virtual knots and long flat virtual knots, especially by combining the long-knot approach of [160] with biquandle constructions, by extracting useful classical-knot invariants from that framework, and by seeking a full classification of long flat knots using the descending-diagram construction D(F) associated to a long flat virtual knot F.
accepted.context_brief: Long virtual and long flat knots

evidence.quote: Enlarge the long knot invariant structure proposed in [160]. Can one get new classical knot invariants from the approach in this paper?
Bring together the ideas from [160] with the biquandle construction from [124] to obtain more powerful invariants of long knots.
It is quite interesting to do sample calculations of such invariants and this situation underlines the deeper problem of finding a full classification of long flat knots.

accepted.question_text: Construct explicit presentations of a virtual biquandle that uses the given linear non-commutative representation at classical crossings together with a genuinely informative algebraic structure at virtual crossings.

evidence.quote: Construct presentations of the virtual biquandle with the a linear (non-commutative) representation at classical crossings and some interesting structure at virtual crossings.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists a birack whose induced action on virtual braids is faithful, and determine whether the invariant for virtual braids cited in [150] is faithful. More broadly, decide whether the known linear actions fail precisely because the corresponding linear invariants of virtual knots and links are not faithful.

evidence.quote: Virtual braids: Is there a birack such that its action on virtual braids is faithful?
Is the invariant of virtual braids in [150], see also [3, 109, 162], faithful?
The action defined by linear biquandles is not faithful.

accepted.question_text: Does the fundamental biquandle classify virtual links up to mirror images, including the known ambiguity that the biquandle has the same value on the orientation-reversed mirror image obtained by reflection in a plane perpendicular to the diagram plane?

evidence.quote: Does the fundamental biquandle, see [124] classify virtual links up to mirror images?
(We know that the biquandle has the same value on the orientation reversed mirror image where the mirror stands perpendicular to the plane (see [64, 65]).

accepted.question_text: Give concrete examples of weak biquandles that are not strong.

evidence.quote: Are there good examples of weak biquandles which are not strong? This problem is solved in [208].

accepted.question_text: Suppose a non-trivial classical knot K is modified by virtualizing some crossings so that the resulting virtual knot K~ is non-trivial and has unit Jones polynomial. Must K~ be non-classical, or could it still be virtually equivalent to a classical knot? More generally, if a virtual knot has unit Jones polynomial, is it equivalent to a classical diagram after virtual equivalence together with crossing virtualization, and if one classical knot can be obtained from another by crossing virtualization plus virtual Reidemeister moves, must the two classical knots already be classically equivalent?

evidence.quote: Suppose the knot K is classical and not trivial. Suppose that K~ (obtained from K by virtualizing a subset of its crossings) is not trivial and has a unit Jones polynomial, V (K~) = 1. Is it possible that K~ is classical (i.e. isotopic through virtual equivalence to a classical knot)?
Suppose K is a virtual knot diagram with unit Jones polynomial. Is K equivalent to a classical diagram via virtual equivalence plus crossing virtualization?
Given two classical knots K and K', if K can be obtained from K' by a combination of crossing virtualization and virtual Reidemeister moves, then is K classically equivalent to K'?

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of virtual quandle homology parallel to existing quandle homology theories and determine what new invariants of virtual knots and links it provides.

evidence.quote: Virtual Quandle Homology: Study virtual quandle homology in analogy to quandle homology [17, 61].

accepted.question_text: Construct a Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual-knot diagrams over the integers, understand the existing constructions that work for large classes of virtual links, and determine structural consequences such as which knots are K-full or Kho-full, whether optimal diagrams are minimal in classical crossing number, and which diagram moves preserve that optimality.

evidence.quote: Construct a generalization of the Khovanov complex for the case of virtual knots that will work for arbitrary virtual diagrams.
The import of our question, is to investigate this structure and to possibly find a way to do Khovanov homology for all virtual knots over the ring of integers.
Classify all K-full (Kho-full) knots.
Are optimal diagrams always minimal with respect to the number of classical crossings?

accepted.question_text: Describe the structure of Jones-Wenzl-type projectors inside the Brauer algebra that arises from adding virtual crossings to the Temperley-Lieb algebra, and determine whether that setting supports a useful algebraic generalization of classical recoupling theory.

evidence.quote: The appropriate domain for the virtual recoupling theory is to place the Jones-Wenzl projectors in the Brauer algebra.
What is the structure of the projectors in this context? Can a useful algebraic generalization of the classical recoupling theory be formulated?

accepted.question_text: Define a notion of alternating virtual knot, classify alternating virtual knots and alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization, and formulate and prove the virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture.

evidence.quote: Virtual Alternating Knots: Define and classify alternating virtual knots. Find an analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture and prove it.
Classify all alternating weaves on surfaces (without stabilization).

accepted.question_text: Find effective methods to prove minimality of crossing number and atom genus for virtual-knot diagrams, including estimates derived from the Kauffman bracket, Thistlethwaite spanning trees, atoms, and Khovanov homology when diagrams are projected not only to the plane but also to higher-genus surfaces.

evidence.quote: Is there is a way to prove that the atom genus g is minimal for a concrete knot diagram?

How do we use the Kauffman bracket, Thistlethwaite spanning tree, atoms and other invariants to get estimates for the number of crossings when projecting the knot diagram not to the plane but rather to some surfaces of higher genera?
Can we get estimates from Thistlethwaite's spanning tree and/or from the Khovanov homology?

accepted.question_text: For a virtual link with minimal classical crossing number C, minimal virtual crossing number V, and minimal total crossing number T, determine how C, V, and T are related, whether T = V + L in the notation of the paper, how the virtual unknotting number behaves, how V relates to minimal genus in a surface representation, and what effective algorithms or polynomial bounds exist for computing or estimating these quantities.

evidence.quote: For each virtual link L, there are three crossing numbers: the minimal number C of classical crossings, the minimal number V of virtual crossings, and the minimal total number T of crossings for representatives of L.
Very little is known. Find out more about the virtual unknotting number.
What is the relationship between the least number of virtual crossings and the least genus in a surface representation of the virtual knot.
Is it true that T = V + L?

accepted.question_text: Formulate a category of wild virtual knots together with an appropriate axiom system, and prove a criterion describing when a wild equivalence between tame virtual links already implies tame equivalence.

evidence.quote: Wild Virtuals: Create the category of 'wild virtual knots' and establish its axiomatics.
In particular, one needs a theorem that states when a wild equivalence of tame virtual links implies a tame equivalence of these links.

accepted.question_text: Understand how virtual-knot polynomials relate to Vassiliev invariants for virtual knots, and determine whether every finite-type Vassiliev invariant of classical knots extends to a finite-type invariant of long virtual knots in the sense described by the paper, while also clarifying the alternate finite-type notion for virtual knots mentioned there.

evidence.quote: Understand the connection between virtual knot polynomials and the Vassiliev knot invariants of virtual knots (in Kauffman's sense).
Does every Vassiliev invariant of finite type, for classical knots extend to an invariant of finite type for long virtual knots?
This alternate formulation needs further investigation.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist classical knots that are not slice in the ordinary classical sense but become slice either in Kauffman's notion of virtual-knot sliceness or in Turaev's notion of sliceness for knots in thickened surfaces, and if a knot in a thickened surface is slice in Turaev's sense, must it stabilize to a virtual knot that is slice in Kauffman's sense?

evidence.quote: Are there any classical knots that are non-slice in the classical sense but are slice in the the sense of Kauffman (when considered as virtual knots) or Turaev (when considered as a knot in a thickened surface)?
If a knot in the thickened surface is slice in the sense of Turaev, does it necessarily stabilize to a virtual knot that is slice in the sense of Kauffman?

accepted.question_text: For the virtual braid group V B_n, determine whether it is linear for all n greater than 3, whether the representation rho: V B_n -> Aut(F_{n+1}) described in the paper is faithful for all n greater than 2, and whether there exist non-equivalent virtual links whose braid closures become equivalent after applying the welded-braid representation rho_A.

evidence.quote: Is it true that V Bn is linear for all n > 3?
Is the representation rho faithful for all n > 2?
Are there some non-equivalent virtual links Lv and L'v that are the closures of the virtual braids ... such that the welded links ... are equivalent as welded links?

accepted.question_text: Prove existence and uniqueness of prime decompositions for long virtual knots, and determine whether the concatenation of two non-classical prime long virtual knots can also be expressed through any essentially different decomposition into the same factors.
accepted.context_brief: Prime decomposition of long virtual knots

evidence.quote: Besides concatenation, there are other kinds of decompositions for long virtual knots.
Prove an existence and uniqueness theorem for prime decompositions of long virtual knots.

accepted.question_text: Extend the theory of virtual covers so that it applies effectively to classical knots in S^3, relate virtual-cover invariants to Milnor mu-invariants and possibly to one-component links, understand how virtual covers behave under local moves such as crossing changes, self-Delta moves, and Z-moves, determine whether virtual covers can detect mutations, and characterize exactly which moves on two-component links preserve the associated virtual-knot type.

evidence.quote: Is there an extension of the theory of virtual covers to one component links (i.e. knots) in S^3.
Use virtual covers to find a relation between the Milnor mu-invariants and invariants of virtual knots.
How well does a virtual knot associated to a virtual cover of a classical link behave under local moves (non-isotopy) applied to the link?
Find a complete set of moves on such two component links which do not change the virtual isotopy type of the associated virtual knot.

Is there any algorithm for recognition whether two graph-links are equivalent or not? Our conjecture is 'no'.

evidence.quote: How can we use this invariant to understand long free knots, or round flat virtual knots, both of which are quotients of long flat virtual knots?
What are braid-like virtual knots topologically?

Extracted explicit numbered problems from Section 8.1, including connected sums, flat virtuals, welded knots, virtual braids, Khovanov homology, crossing numbers, wild virtuals, and Vassiliev invariants.
Extracted additional explicit questions from Sections 8.2.4, 8.3, 8.5.2, and 8.5.3, and flagged some later clusters for further atomization in needs_review.
